newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Jewish attack suspects had bomb site maps.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Jewish attack suspects had bomb site maps.

text.p: Four suspects arrested for a weekend attack on a Jewish cemetery had floor plans of a Jewish centre razed by a bomb and maps showing how many Jews there are in each Argentine province, a judge said on Friday.

"It is suspicious that these people should have such things," Judge Victor Termite told a radio station, referring to the men arrested on Thursday. He said the maps were among documents seized in overnight raids after the desecration of 100 graves at La Tablada, Argentina's largest Jewish cemetery, in the outskirts of Buenos Aires.

The attackers smashed and marked tombstones with swastikas and daubbed the site with graffiti calling the Nazi Holocaust "a great Jewish lie." The suspects claimed to belong to nationalistic organisations that Jewish community members say are well-known right-wing, anti-Semitic groups.

"I really don't know if this is connected with any active participation in the AMIA attack," Termite said of the car bombing that razed the AMIA Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires in July 1994, killing 86 people.
The bombing, the worst peacetime attack on Jews since the Second World War, is in the hands of another judge.

Also on Friday morning, an anonymous caller phoned the Israelite Hospital in Buenos Aires to say a bomb would go off at 9:53 A.M. -- the same time the AMIA car bomb went off. Police found nothing. It was the third such threat this week and the second against the hospital.

Argentina's Jewish community, one of the largest in the world, has suffered at least five cemetery desecrations in the last few years. And in 1992 the Israeli Embassy was destroyed by a car bomb that killed 29 people.

Bet El, a leading Argentine Jewish group, on Tuesday blamed "Nazis in the state's repressive apparatus" for the desecrations and called the local Jewish community "the most vulnerable in the world." Argentina's best-known human rights group, the Mothers of Plaza de Mayo, demonstrated against the incidents outside the government house on Thursday.

Argentine security services have been criticised by the Jewish community, Israel and the United States for failing to find the authors of the bomb attacks, which have been blamed on the Iranian-backed Moslem fundamentalist Hizbollah group.
